date_note: Informburo's 24 November report gives no earlier day for the listing or the briefing.
exec: A seller claims to hold Supreme Court of Kazakhstan data on 16.6 million citizens; officials are checking it and nothing is confirmed.
plain: A seller on a dark web marketplace claims to have a Supreme Court of Kazakhstan database on 16.6 million citizens. Officials say they are checking whether the claim is true.

sources.name: Informburo: Минцифры и КНБ проверяют информацию о возможной утечке данных Верховного суда
The Times of Central Asia: Kazakhstan Data Leak Claims Involving 16.6 Million People Under Investigation

evidence.quote: утверждал, что она содержит 507 млн записей за период с 2014 по 2026 годы
that allegedly contains personal information on 16.6 million citizens.
The seller claims to have gained access to data from Kazakhstan’s Supreme Court and is asking $50,000 for the database.

summary: Informburo and The Times of Central Asia report that SOCRadar found a dark web listing of a database that allegedly contains personal information on 16.6 million citizens; the seller claims it comes from the Supreme Court of Kazakhstan and asks $50,000. Minister Zhaslan Madiyev said a check is under way; the claim is unverified.
title: Seller claims Supreme Court of Kazakhstan database; ministry and KNB checking

validation.note: Informburo and The Times of Central Asia read; both relay the seller's claim, SOCRadar's finding and the ministry's check; nothing is confirmed.

review.note: summary: check by ministry with KNB restated closer to Informburo; other facts match
